lines: A four-voice sequence generator built on four internal tracks clocked at different divisions, after Orca, the alternative firmware for monome's White Whale
Sets how many steps the sequence runs before returning to its first step, 1 to 32
Sets the rate of the internal clock in BPM, 20 to 2000, and sets the beat that GATE LEN multiplies to give the length of a note gate
Sets the clock division and starting count of each of the four internal tracks, 0 to 127, and so the polyrhythm the whole sequence is built from
Sets how notes and gates are drawn from the four internal tracks, 0 to 127: the upper bits choose which tracks add to a note value and which of sixteen gate patterns is used
Moves the sequence up the scale by this many notes, 0 to 12; above 6 each note output is moved one further step than the one before it
Chooses one of sixteen patterns of silenced steps, 0 to 15, holding the note gates at 0V on the steps that pattern covers
Adds to every note CV output, -2V to 2V, moving the sequence up or down by as much as two octaves
Sets how long a note gate stays open, as a multiple of one beat of SPEED from 0.1 to 4
Switches between the two scales, A and B, on each press; the A and B lamps show which one is in use
Raises the note CV outputs by one octave while scale A is the one in use, and comes up pressed on a new module
Raises the note CV outputs by one octave while scale B is the one in use, and comes up unpressed on a new module
Switches that note in or out of scale A; the sequence takes its pitches only from the notes switched in
Switches that note in or out of scale B; the sequence takes its pitches only from the notes switched in
Adds to the LENGTH knob, 10V covering the whole of its travel, with the total held between 1 and 32 steps
Adds to the SPEED knob, 10V covering the whole of its travel, with the total held between 20 and 2000 BPM
Adds to the ALGO X knob, 10V covering the whole of its travel, with the total held between 0 and 127
Adds to the ALGO Y knob, 10V covering the whole of its travel, with the total held between 0 and 127
Adds to the SHIFT knob, 10V covering the whole of its travel, with the total held between 0 and 12 notes
Adds to the SPACE knob, 10V covering the whole of its travel, with the total held between 0 and 15
Adds to the TRANSPOSE knob at 2.5V per octave, with the total held between -2V and 2V
Adds to the GATE LEN knob, 10V covering the whole of its travel, with the total held between 0.1 and 4
Switches between scale A and scale B on each rising edge above 2V
Raises the note CV outputs by one octave while scale A is in use and this reads any voltage above 0V; a negative voltage here cancels the + OCTAVE A button
Raises the note CV outputs by one octave while scale B is in use and this reads any voltage above 0V; a negative voltage here cancels the +OCTAVE B button
Steps the sequence on each rising edge above 2V, and patching a cable here stops the internal clock
Returns the sequence to its first step on a rising edge above 2V, and fires the RESET output
Nothing in the module reads this jack; the maker configures it as Expansion 1 (unused) and left it for a future expander
Nothing in the module reads this jack; the maker configures it as Expansion 2 (unused) and left it for a future expander
A 1ms 10V pulse on each step of the sequence, whether the step came from the internal clock or from the CLOCK input
A 1ms 10V pulse each time the sequence returns to its first step, either after LENGTH steps or from a trigger at the RESET input
The pitch of that voice, 1V per octave: the scale note the algorithm chose for it, plus its octave, plus TRANSPOSE and the octave button of the scale in use
Carries 10V while that voice's note is sounding and 0V otherwise; the gate reopens only when the note changes, and is held at 0V on the steps SPACE silences
One of four stepped voltages worked out from which internal tracks are on, 0V to 10V in eight steps, changing on each step of the sequence
Carries 10V while its internal track is on and 0V while that track is off, changing on each step of the sequence
Note — with nothing patched to CLOCK the sequence runs from an internal clock at the rate SPEED sets; patching a cable there stops that clock and steps the sequence on each rising edge instead
Note — a scale with no notes switched in produces nothing: every note CV output reads 0V and every note gate stays at 0V. Scale A comes up with C, D and E switched in and scale B comes up empty
Note — the screen reads out the eight main parameters as numbers, including the values the CV inputs have added, so it shows what the sequence is actually running on

SDOrcasHeart.notes: Written from the maker's source at commit 70a282a76d3a6da7fb84dd45aa1e4670538a951e, the commit that first carries version 2.0.4 in plugin.json. Two later commits also carry 2.0.4 and both add a second module, SDLines, and a redrawn SDOrcasHeartV2; the installed plugin.json lists only SDOrcasHeart, the installed res directory holds exactly the files res held at 70a282a (SDOrcasHeart.svg through SDOrcasHeart6.svg, sd_switch1_1_.svg, sd_scale_o2_1.svg — all moved to dev/shared_components in the later commits), and strings on the installed plugin.dylib finds res/SDOrcasHeart6.svg with no trace of SDLines or of its Horizontal/Vertical menu wording. So 70a282a is what shipped. EXP 1 and EXP 2 are configured as inputs, given jacks on the panel and never read anywhere in process(); the maker's own names for them say (unused), so both get a line saying nothing reads them. The module is monophonic throughout: every read is getVoltage() with no channel and every write is setVoltage() with no channel. The eight parameter CV inputs all go through one function, getValue(), which scales the jack by the parameter's span over 10V, adds the knob and clamps the total to the parameter's own range — so 10V always covers the whole of a knob's travel whatever the units, and a negative voltage subtracts until the total hits the knob's floor. The clock, reset and scale-switch jacks all use rescale(v, 0.1f, 2.f, 0.f, 1.f) into a default SchmittTrigger, which makes the rising threshold 2V and the falling threshold 0.1V. The two octave buttons are read through getValue() as well, so their jacks are level-sensed rather than edge-triggered: any voltage above 0V turns the octave on, and a negative voltage cancels a pressed button. The wiki says the CV inputs expect a 10V range quoted as -5V to +5V or 0V to +10V; the code takes any voltage and clamps the sum, so a bipolar cable works but only the part of it that moves the total inside the knob's range has any effect. The twelve scale switches of each scale share one line each, since they differ only in which note they switch in. The A and B lamps are lights rather than parameters and cannot be clicked for help.
